column1: SCORING ARCHITECTURE

86 items administered. Three composite T-scores from intact published short forms: PROMIS Physical Function SF 20a (20 items), PROMIS Upper Extremity SF 7a (7 items), Neuro-QOL Upper Extremity Fine Motor/ADL SF (8 items) - 35 scored responses from 32 administered items, because PFA55 and PFB26 each feed PF 20a + Neuro-QOL, and PFA34 feeds PF 20a + UE 7a. Score each form with its published raw-score-to-T-score lookup table (HealthMeasures).
23 bank add-on items are calibrated PROMIS/Neuro-QOL items used descriptively (unscored). They are legitimate to administer standalone; do not add them to the short-form raw scores.
31 supplemental items (SUP-) are non-validated screeners written in PROMIS style. Report qualitatively. Never combine with T-scores.
Color key in Source column: blue = PF 20a, green = UE 7a, yellow = Neuro-QOL UE (or shared), grey = bank add-on, orange = supplemental.
DESIGN DECISIONS

PF 20a chosen over PF 24a (PROMIS-HAQ) as the scored backbone: the two share 6 items and measure the same construct, 20a has the cleaner pure-PF lookup table, and the 24a's unique ADL content (feeding, bed transfer, walking a block) is restored via bank add-ons PFA20, PFB29r1, PFC53, PFC6r1.

Domains with no PROMIS coverage anywhere (confirmed against all 176 bank items): sitting tolerance, cervical function, typing, driving, continence, all five senses, sleep, sexual function. These are supplemental by necessity, per the agreed screener-only approach.

Gaps filled bank-first per instruction. The one deliberate exception: floor-to-waist lifting uses graded supplemental SUP-29 rather than bank item PFM38 (50-lb sand bag), which floors out for impaired respondents; PFM38 remains available if bank purity is preferred.
Administration: self-report, paper or verbal. Estimated completion 12-18 minutes. Items grouped by section and response scale to reduce respondent burden.
OA-Knee SF 13a is not included; append it unchanged as a condition-specific module for knee claims (13 items, own score).
